correctness.rationale: For labeled squared moduli and positive radii, the four normalized quarter-turn outputs separate the constant, complex first harmonic and real alternating term. Distinct u_j=r_j² kill H_10 and H_21 in the kernel; the two alternating projections kill H_20 exactly when sin(2(θ₂−θ₁))≠0. The remaining kernel is generated by diag(u₁u₂,−u₁−u₂,1), which is invertible, whereas aa*−bb* has rank at most two. Equal radii give the ambiguity z² versus r², and the resonant rotations give 1±i·exp(−2iθ₁)z² because exp(−2iθ₁)z² is real at every sample. For seven or fewer measurements a spanning scheme leaves a real Hermitian kernel plane, whose odd determinant has a nonzero singular zero; spanning excludes nonzero semidefinite matrices in that kernel, so an indefinite rank-two matrix gives an ambiguity. A nonspanning scheme fails already against zero. For the eight lattice samples, an independent exact reconstruction of the real Frobenius-orthonormal lift Q/2 gave rank eight, K=diag(2,−3,1), and row-Gram characteristic polynomial (t−8)(t−2)(t²−24t+14)(t²−12t+2)², establishing all multiplicities and normalization. By the rank-two trace bound the squared projection of a rank-two H onto K⊥ is at least ||H||²/14, yielding the displayed uniform factor using the least positive squared singular value 6−√34. No sharpness of this factor is asserted. Independent replay with Python and SymPy: /workspace/branches/1cb84397-f935-4693-91aa-c5179a235da0/independent_spectrum.py. The frozen check.py and check_output.txt were inspected, not executed; the finite computation does not establish the arbitrary-radii result or the universal minimum, which use the analytic arguments.
